boundaries: All 86 packages and 387 modules remain in scope: 46 complete packages, 199 complete modules and 228 incomplete units. I/O workflows lie outside these algorithm-family entries. No family is invented or promoted.

Native JSON/XML/CSV/SQLite readers, writers and other algorithms are unchanged. All 167 verified core objects are reused; server, CLI and four assertion-enabled I/O suites are freshly built. Server changes wire existing options, optional standard opening documents and the native public paired CSV file writer. Other algorithm proofs remain inherited.

All exports use the current original uploaded File bytes without JavaScript parse/stringify conversion. Reports bind every actual input and each downloaded output by name, size and SHA-256. Import JSON responses preserve numeric tokens in complete records and standard opening files. Native source-type inference/conversion remains an independent parity gate.

Classic and standard import choices retain their requested native variant names while the native readers autodetect supported envelopes. Wrong format/source and malformed data remain explicit native errors. Guards validate envelopes; they do not establish complete schema/dialect parity.

include_open_source=true adds a standard source serialized from the same imported native result. Ordinary import response shapes are unchanged without it. All six simple imports and five rich imports pass additive-shape and full actual-import standard-source roundtrip checks. The rich browser handoff retains sixteen relation-feature rows and the actual duplicated #2 identifier suffix.

Native rich roundtrip retains full data for standard JSON, both XML formats and SQLite. Classic JSON reimport normalizes repeated event/object pairs, yielding fifteen instead of sixteen controlled relations. That existing format convention stays a gate; the core parser is unchanged. Broader schema/type/dialect/ordering/attribute/platform and exact byte conventions remain open.

Paired CSV export parses the original source once, calls the native public two-file writer, reads exact binary streams and removes owned temporary files on success or rejection. It retains object attributes and orphan objects without opting into loss. Native event-only export still rejects object attributes unless loss is explicitly allowed. CSV globals/qualifiers/O2O/E2E/changes are unsupported; loss allowance does not bypass duplicate relation or structural errors.

XML declaration, unsupported-construct rejection and byte-limit controls drive existing native options. Writer loss allowance does not bypass JSON-source reference validation, so dangling JSON sources still fail before writing. The UI states that limitation. SQLite readable type names and reference validation drive existing native options; type-table and typed int64 data are inspected in actual databases.

CSV column/prefix names preserve literal whitespace, punctuation and Unicode. Delimiters match the native single-byte contract, with a single backslash-plus-t for tab. CSV requires header rows. Other header/quoting/escaping/inferred-type/order/error and size-limit behaviors remain independent gates.

Complete positional inspection retains actual native arrays/maps and each repeated relation position. All-row CSV is independently compared with complete native records, including thirty events/relations, thirty-one objects, orphan objects and full int64 values. Text preview is explicitly limited to 6000 characters; download bytes remain complete. Empty imports retain standard documents/CSV schema but opening is disabled.

Existing JSON/SQLite export adapters now accept original Blob/File bytes and preserve native numeric tokens when supplied parsed native records. Standard JSON export guard accepts actual arrays. Older import adapters and other transport/default/error conventions remain independent gates; the new workflow itself consumes raw native JSON.

Cancellation signals and source guards have unit coverage without a claim of native computation interruption or a browser race-cancellation success. File selection and active-source changes reset imported results; native errors retain the preceding complete result. Landing and classic imports do not require an active OCEL.

The final phone correction changes only styles.css. All behavior JavaScript bytes remain identical between the final behavior capture build and the final layout build, although Vite renames the main asset after CSS changes. Current served JS/CSS bytes are verified against the final build; both form sets and the new header fit a 390px viewport.

Retained captures record incomplete unit fixture arrays, native rich CSV duplicate rejection despite loss consent, source validation before XML allowance, actual duplicate row suffixes, delimiter-label escaping, phone header overflow and a Vite filename-versus-content assumption. Each correction uses fresh helper/output namespaces; no reference bodies/bytecode were inspected.

Final evidence binds 802 frontend tests, four fresh native suites, 74 primary checks over 69 HTTP calls/13 CLI runs, five control/pagination checks over seven calls, 34 browser checks and 45 artifact/report/CSV/database/asset checks. Eleven CSV artifacts and nine native file downloads are independently bound. Owned server/tab are closed, viewport restored and port 8497 released. Remaining model/export and acquisition workflows and full exactness/performance gates continue.
